Battlefield Earth is one of the best space operas you can hope to read (LRH is a huge POS otherwise and deserves to burn in 7 hells for all eternity because of Scientology). He had a gift for turning out page after page of clever dross that rarely bogged down or became tedious. Anyhow so I'm going to stick with modern writers: Neal Stephenson is my favorite. His ability to flesh out and make characters interesting, in some really intriguing settings, sets him apart. Cryptonomicon is probably my favorite book of all time. It's like 600 pages and I don't think I put it down once I started reading.

Someone else mentioned Gene Wolfe who IMO is vastly under appreciated. Every page reminds you of how intelligent a writer he is, but not in a showy way. There's a subtle yet brutal flavor to his writing.

And then there's Philip Jose Farmer. Riverworld was pretty great afterall, plus all his short stuff. At the time you couldn't get swearing published so he wrote a story that included, as a part of the plot, Fuck You in ASCII and got it published. Just getting a ASCII chart in the 70s was a trick so even though it seems lame today at the time is was clever, racy stuff. At least I think it was Farmer that did this.

And of course Robert Sheckley for his fantastically creative wackiness. His longer works usually fell off the rails towards the end but his collection of short stories are still a treasure of hilarious inventive scenarios. Look for a copy of Can You Feel Anything When I do This? the next time you're browsing the stacks at a used book store.

What is "you" and what is consciousness? Also, what does "upload" mean? In all current interpretations of the word, "upload" does not mean to move data from client to server, it means to copy data. When we think of "uploading" ourselves into a robot body, we think of transferring that experience of the eternal present, that thing we think of as "us" even though there's no real reason to believe that's us- that could just be the universe thinking it's us. Or it may be us, but be irrevocably bound to this body.

Also, when you upload yourself, what happens to your current body/mind? Is is destroyed in the process? If so, did you upload yourself, or did you kill yourself in order to create an electronic doppelganger? If your brain/mind isn't destroyed in the process, did you just create a doppelganger which thinks it's you, and is probably somewhat hostile to this other thing that would still think it's the real you?

To what end? This touches on the question "What is consciousness?" and I'm not sure an android brain would be complete enough to emulate a human properly.

Example: are we just exporting the "memory"? If so, then what's the point? A human without the ability to interact with its environment, understand its sense of self in the world, sense emotion immediately, engage in situations and affect others is not really a conscious human. Exporting just the memory means you'd have a lot of data but not much to do with it.

The "what is consciousness" question needs to be tackled first in order to make this worthwhile. Otherwise, I would rather just export a human memory into book form
